claims_policy.rights_claims: Only license expressions already declared by repository manifests are recorded. A declaration is not treated as proof that a matching notice has been supplied.
claims_policy.retail_content: Retail executables, PDBs, data, scripts, replays, art, audio, raw/bulk live captures, and content packs derived from them are not release payloads. A deliberately tracked compact redacted fact/protocol record may be source evidence, never a grant to redistribute underlying content.
claims_policy.blocked_means: The named release claim is refused until the missing artifact is added and this manifest is deliberately updated.
claims_policy.proved_means: The evidence proves only the gate's narrow claim, not whole-product readiness.

license_text_catalog.evidence: The tracked text identifies itself as GNU General Public License Version 3, 29 June 2007; repository manifests separately select the -or-later expression where declared.

gates.claim: Every discovered repository Cargo manifest or remote workspace template carries applicable tracked license text for its declared expression.
gates.blocker: tools/owned-peer declares MIT and tools/oracle/remote-Cargo.toml declares MIT OR Apache-2.0, but this proof pack found no applicable tracked texts and does not infer them. Obtain exact notices/texts from an authoritative source or change declarations with authority.

gates.claim: Every remote workspace template preserves the repository workspace's effective license expression unless a separately authorized exception is proved.
gates.blocker: The repository workspace declares GPL-3.0-or-later, while the oracle workspace template copied to hbox declares MIT OR Apache-2.0 and supplies inherited metadata to copied crates. The proof pack records the inconsistency rather than choosing a license.

gates.claim: A whole-tree inventory accounts for non-Cargo source, documentation, generated code, vendored material, exceptions, notices, and applicable license text.
gates.blocker: The Cargo declaration inventory is not a whole-source provenance inventory. Expected reviewed artifact: release/source-license-inventory.json.

gates.claim: The current source-release tooling refuses its enumerated local/proprietary roots, generated-output paths, file formats/signatures, known executable hash, and compact-evidence violations, with explicit git-archive exclusions.
The public source archive builds the exact checked-in binary candidate without retail/live-derived inputs, and the candidate is byte-linked to that build.
gates.blocker: An isolated git-archive build fails at crates/don-sim/src/systems/leaders.rs because its include_str! compile-time dependency on schema/live/live-tables-unit.tsv is correctly export-ignored. The checked-in browser Wasm therefore is not reproducible from the public source projection. Replace the compile-time dependency with an explicit fail-closed runtime/content authority boundary; do not redistribute the live TSV.

gates.claim: Every PDB/binary/live-derived fact extract admitted to a public source release has a reviewed classification and redistribution rationale distinct from rejection of raw PDB/PE content.
gates.blocker: The source audit denies known raw formats and paths but does not inventory or adjudicate tracked derived research tables. Expected reviewed artifact: release/derived-research-review.json.

gates.claim: Every dependency conveyed in a binary product has an audited license expression, required notice/text, and source treatment bound to the exact assembled artifact/SBOM and its contributing lock identities.
gates.blocker: A component-only precursor binds the checked-in browser Wasm to its five-package lock graph and captures the two registry packages' declarations/texts, while the source-archive probe proves that candidate is not yet reproducible from distributable source. All five records remain pending human obligation/source-treatment review; the graph is not a linked-code SBOM, and no exact assembled-product payload identifies the conveyed subset. Expected completion artifact: release/product-dependency-notices.json.

gates.claim: A local, create-only bootstrap verifies one retail executable identity and 51 owned data/script inputs before writing only ignored ron-data destinations; it is not a product installer or redistribution path.
A user can install, configure, repair, and remove a complete standalone DoN product from an exact release payload.
gates.blocker: The repository explicitly describes a source development snapshot and owned-data bootstrap, not a standalone product installer; no product payload/repair/uninstall manifest is in this proof pack.

gates.claim: Every shipped art, audio, font, and presentation-data item has item-level provenance, license/extraction status, attribution, content identity, and the required human clearance recorded without the tooling certifying legal title.
gates.blocker: A fail-closed mechanical content-manifest auditor now exists and explicitly emits legal_title_certified=false, but no real non-empty independent pack, human rights review, in-product attribution proof, or distribution clearance record is supplied. This pack records no license for any retail asset.

gates.claim: The active-solo controller lifecycle has a compact machine record for five consecutive main-thread STOP/rearm acknowledgements plus a final park, zero dropped events, and an independent external read of the exact original five call bytes after every STOP.
gates.blocker: The measured five-cycle result is recorded in hash-bound prose, but the public tree has no compact per-cycle machine artifact. The older incident JSON explicitly predates and does not prove the active-main-thread path. Expected artifact: schema/live/retail-control-active-stop-cycles-v1.json.

gates.claim: The tree contains a scoped WER workflow and synthetic regression cases for exact-owned setup/removal, dump preservation, and stable in-place MDMP verification without copying dumps.

The recorded STOP-associated incident is closed by candidate-bound active soak/reversibility evidence; if another crash naturally occurs, its stable retained minidump identity and stack analysis are added without requiring an intentional crash.
gates.blocker: The incident record states dump_retained=false and explicitly declines to claim a unique cause. Successful later runs need a compact candidate-bound incident-closure/soak record; a new crash is not required. Expected artifact: schema/live/retail-control-stop-incident-closure-v1.json.

gates.claim: Public release status documents agree on active STOP/rearm and real-host lobby-peering status.
gates.blocker: README.md still says the active STOP/rearm exercise is missing, and docs/tooling/live-control.md says real-host peering remains open, while GOAL.md records both as green at their bounded scopes.

gates.claim: An exact assembled product payload, checksums, dependency notices, independent-content clearance, install/repair/remove behavior, and a product-specific allowlisted provenance audit are recorded together.
gates.blocker: There is no assembled product payload manifest or product-specific allowlisted provenance audit. The checked-in Wasm also cannot yet be reproduced from the public source archive because an export-ignored live table is a compile-time input. The existing release-audit.sh is intentionally source-only and rejects executable payloads, so it cannot admit a binary product tree.
